title: Massive quantum divergence on the Cauchy horizon of a black hole
authors: Marc Casals, Lorenzo Pisani, Peter Taylor
abstract: We investigate a quantum massive scalar field in the interior of a charged and spherically-symmetric (Reissner-Nordström) black hole. We examine the behaviour for varying values of the black hole charge, field mass and coupling constant when the field is in two quantum states: Hartle-Hawking (representing a black hole in thermal equilibrium) and Unruh (representing a black hole evaporating via the emission of Hawking radiation). We show that the vacuum polarization as well as the angular components of the quantum stress-energy tensor diverge on the Cauchy horizon, in stark contrast to what happens for massless fields. We also calculate the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $\{u,v\}$. We show that these fluxes on the Cauchy horizon do not generically vanish. This implies, in particular, that in regular, Kruskal coordinates $\{U,V\}$ the ingoing flux diverges like $V^{-2}$ on the Cauchy horizon (where $V=0$). This divergence suggests that its backreaction via the semiclassical Einstein equations would yield a strong singularity, as opposed to its weaker, classical counterpart. Interestingly, there are exceptions, in which the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates vanish: (i) in the extremal limit (where the black hole is maximally charged); (ii) certain fine-tuned regions of parameter space, where the fluxes change sign.
summary: This paper analyzes quantum fluctuations of a massive scalar field inside a charged black hole, specifically focusing on the Cauchy horizon. The key finding is that quantum effects cause divergences in the stress-energy tensor on the CH, suggesting a stronger singularity than classical theory predicts. This work probes the limits of semi-classical gravity in extreme astrophysical environments.
main_problem: The study investigates the behavior of quantum massive scalar fields near the Cauchy horizon (CH) of a charged Reissner-Nordström black hole, focusing on quantum divergences and their implications for spacetime structure.
main_result: The vacuum polarization and stress-energy tensor components diverge on the CH for massive fields, suggesting a strong singularity via backreaction, unlike the classical prediction.
method: The authors employ a semi-classical approach, calculating renormalized expectation values of quantum fields using techniques like the extended coordinate method in curved spacetime.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum massive scalar field propagating in the interior of a charged, spherically-symmetric Reissner-Nordström black hole spacetime.

important_parameters: Black hole charge ($Q$), field mass ($\mu$), coupling constant ($\xi$), and the choice of quantum state (Hartle-Hawking vs. Unruh).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the RN background and relies on the semi-classical approximation where quantum effects source classical spacetime curvature.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the divergence of vacuum polarization and stress-energy tensor components near the CH for varying field masses and charges, and show the dependence of fluxes on parameters.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the quantum field behavior by comparing massive and massless cases, calculating divergences in the vacuum polarization and stress-energy tensor components, and discussing the implications for the stability and singularity structure of the Cauchy horizon.
why_interesting: While focused on general relativity, the study of divergences and backreaction in extreme spacetime geometries shares conceptual parallels with understanding instabilities or strong coupling regimes in quantum many-body systems.
